name: Scale-Invariant Integral Surface Rendering
aliases: method using homothetic distance and quadratic polynomial interpolation
definition: A rendering algorithm for scale-invariant integral surfaces that reduces computation time by using a new initial sampling strategy based on homothetic distance to segment primitives, a field mapping combined with quadratic polynomial interpolation, and an efficient GPU implementation using an A-buffer.
summary: Scale-Invariant Integral Surface Rendering is a GPU-accelerated ray marching algorithm that reduces grazing ray step counts using homothetic distance sampling and quadratic polynomial interpolation.
